newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile's Enami begins wage talks at copper plant.
newsitem.headline: Chile's Enami begins wage talks at copper plant.

text.p: Chile's state mining company Enami said it has started collective wage negotiations with unions at the firm's Ventanas copper smelter and refinery.
"Workers handed over their pay demands yesterday," vice president Claudio Agostini told reporters.
Talks will take place over the next six weeks to renew the existing labor contract which runs out January 31, he said.
Workers at the plant went on strike for 10 days two years ago after the last round of scheduled wage talks broke down.
Ventanas, which lies on the central Chilean coast, smelts 126,000 tonnes of copper a year and has a refining capacity of 330,000 tonnes.
Workers at Enami's Paipote smelter voted last month to accept the company's terms for a five year collective contract.
